title: Windows Time Source Discovery, DNS, Holdover, and Advertising Warnings
exclusions: Reports Microsoft-Windows-Time-Service System events 36, 129, 134, and 142 during a closed 15-minute window. It does not measure clock offset, assert a five-second Kerberos threshold, prove authentication failure, identify all time-service events, query W32Time state, or distinguish transient recovery without follow-up. Event 129 is domain-peer discovery failure; 134 is manual-peer DNS resolution failure; 36 reports prolonged lack of usable timestamps using message/configuration values; 142 means the server stopped advertising because its clock was unsynchronized. No automatic W32Time reset, runtime validation, compliance, or SME assurance is claimed.
evidence: Retain saved search `windows_time_service_warnings`, schedule/dispatch/alert history, each raw event row with host/Event ID/message/record ID, matching System XML, authorized `w32tm /query /status /verbose`, `/source`, `/configuration`, and `/peers` output, role/PDC inventory, source health, input/add-on versions, controls, alert delivery, disposition, and bounded exception. This documentation review ran no command, event, search, or remediation.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Insert one XML System event in the closed window with `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `Provider_Name=Microsoft-Windows-Time-Service`, `EventCode=134`, `Computer=DC01.example`, `EventRecordID=9001`, and message naming `time.example` with error `0x80072AF9`. Expect one `manual_peer_dns_resolution_failed` row for `dc01.example`, preserving peer/error/message and record ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for provider `Kernel-General` ID 36, Time-Service ID 35, an event in the newest excluded five minutes, or missing host. Confirm 129, 134, 36, and 142 retain distinct documented meanings and are not relabelled `time difference too large` or `time service stopped`.

dataSources: Windows System XML from provider `Microsoft-Windows-Time-Service`, Event IDs 36, 129, 134, 142, collected with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) as `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`, deployment-local `index=wineventlog`. Required fields are `_time`, `Computer`/`host`, provider, `EventCode`/`EventID`, `EventRecordID`, `Level`, and `Message`; peer, retry interval, and error text are event-version/message dependent.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), reviewed at 10.0.1; no premium app required.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode IN (36,129,134,142) earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_id=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), provider=lower(trim(coalesce(Provider_Name,SourceName))), host=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,dest,host))), message=coalesce(Message,RenderedDescription,_raw)
| where provider="microsoft-windows-time-service" AND event_id IN (36,129,134,142) AND len(host)>0
| eval issue=case(event_id=36,"no_usable_timestamp_during_holdover",event_id=129,"domain_peer_discovery_failed",event_id=134,"manual_peer_dns_resolution_failed",event_id=142,"stopped_advertising_clock_unsynchronized")
| rex field=message max_match=1 "(?i)(?<error_code>0x[0-9a-f]{8})"
| rex field=message max_match=1 "(?i)(?:peer|source).*?'(?<peer>[^']+)'"
| eval error_code=lower(coalesce(error_code,"not_extracted")), peer=coalesce(peer,"not_extracted")
| table _time host event_id issue error_code peer EventRecordID Level source sourcetype message
| sort 0 -_time host event_id
description: Reports one row per selected Windows Time Service warning in the closed interval from 20 to 5 minutes before dispatch, at host/event grain. Each row preserves Microsoft's event-specific issue class, error/peer when extractable, record identity, level, source, and full message for role-aware time hierarchy triage.
value: Reliable domain time underpins Kerberos authentication, domain-controller replication, and trustworthy event sequencing. Correctly distinguishing discovery, DNS, holdover, and advertising warnings directs teams toward peer configuration, DNS/network reachability, hierarchy, virtualization, or server-role investigation without destructive blanket service resets. This reduces authentication and timeline risk by exposing named Windows Time warnings before they become widespread.
implementation: Collect System XML from all Windows servers and domain controllers, validate provider/fields, and save `windows_time_service_warnings`. Run every 15 minutes over a five-minute delayed closed window; alert on any row, with DC/PDC and 142 prioritized. Use authorized `w32tm` queries and message-specific Microsoft guidance before changing peers, service, registry, firewall, or Hyper-V integration.
visualization: Show System-source freshness, warnings by event ID and host role, a timeline, and a table with peer/error/message. Drilldown should include exact XML, current source/status/configuration and adjacent Time-Service/Kernel-General events; never display these warnings as measured clock skew.
dataModelAcceleration: No Change CIM substitute preserves Time-Service event/message/peer/error semantics. Keep raw events; any summary requires parity and source-health proof.

knownFalsePositives:
Rows are genuine warnings; determine whether they are transient/approved.

1. **Windows Update or planned reboot** — Verify change, boot/service timeline, source reacquisition and current `w32tm` status. Use an expiring host/change exception only after recovery.

2. **Active Directory site/DC maintenance** — Domain-peer discovery can fail while DCs are drained. Match site, DC Locator/DNS evidence, maintenance owner and end time; never permanently suppress 129.

3. **DNS maintenance for manual NTP peers** — Confirm DNS change, exact peer, resolver evidence and recovered 134. Scope exception to host/peer/event/window.

4. **Hyper-V migration or VM time-provider test** — Correlate Hyper-V integration settings, VM move, PDC role, event 35/37 and approved test; preserve 142.

5. **PDC emulator transfer or quorum/DR exercise** — Verify FSMO transfer, hierarchy plan, peer/status before and after, and exercise ID.

**Safe suppression:** apply post-result `lookup windows_time_notification_exceptions.csv` by exact `host,event_id,peer,exception_id` with owner/approver/reason and numeric validity bounds; reject wildcards and open-ended rows.
mitreAttack: N/A (Windows time reliability monitoring; no ATT&CK behavior asserted)
hardware: Windows systems using W32Time, especially AD DS domain controllers and the forest-root PDC emulator. Role inventory is required for severity.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Microsoft W32Time event, tool, hierarchy and troubleshooting documentation plus Splunk Windows add-on documentation; events, commands, SPL, controls, alerting, offset, hierarchy, and remediation not executed or SME-signed

cost.search_load_notes: Four low-volume provider-specific System event IDs over 15 closed minutes.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and meaning

Assign AD/time, Windows, virtualization, DNS/network, Splunk and incident owners. Inventory domain members, DCs, forest-root PDC, manual peers, virtualization integration and source-health coverage. Deploy `Splunk_TA_windows` (Splunkbase 742); the search role needs read-only `index=wineventlog` access.

Microsoft documents W32Time as essential to Kerberos and AD DS replication. Do not invent event meanings: 129 is domain-peer discovery error; 134 manual-peer DNS resolution error; 36 says no provider supplied a usable timestamp for the message's holdover period; 142 says advertising stopped because the local clock is not synchronized. None directly measures offset. Use `w32tm /stripchart` or approved monitoring for offset.

## Collect and verify

Enable XML System collection in governed `local/inputs.conf` with `[WinEventLog://System]`, `renderXml=true`, `index=wineventlog`, `checkpointInterval=5`. Validate `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` and `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`; prevent direct/WEF duplicates and preserve Computer. Check representative fields:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:System" earliest=-24h
| eval provider=lower(coalesce(Provider_Name,SourceName))
| where provider="microsoft-windows-time-service"
| table _time Computer EventCode EventRecordID Level Message
```

Compare EventRecordIDs with Event Viewer on a member, DC and PDC. Test localized message extraction; `not_extracted` must retain the event. Monitor feed freshness separately.

## Schedule and controls

Save `windows_time_service_warnings`, run every 15 minutes with `earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m`, and trigger on any row. Measure ingestion latency and adjust closed windows without overlap. Route 142 on a DC/PDC and recurring 36/129/134 urgently through enrichment outside the base SPL. Never use the old false labels.

Replay positive/negative fixtures and boundary times. Assert provider collision protection, exact issue mapping, peer/error preservation, missing-host rejection, and newest-window exclusion. In a lab, use approved invalid peer/DNS scenarios and restore configuration; do not disrupt production domain time. Record OS/add-on/Splunk versions, GPO/configuration, XML, exact bounds, expected/actual rows, job ID and delivery. Keep draft until owners accept runtime behavior.

## Triage and response

Verify raw event/source freshness and host role. With authorization run `w32tm /query /status /verbose`, `/source`, `/configuration`, and `/peers`; compare effective GPO/registry source, DNS and UDP 123 reachability, domain hierarchy, PDC configuration, and Hyper-V time provider. Microsoft documents `/resync /rediscover`, but run it only under the Windows/AD owner after evidence capture. For 142 follow Microsoft's role/configuration/virtualization-specific guidance.

Do not automatically unregister/register W32Time, edit registry, change AnnounceFlags, disable VM time integration, open firewall, transfer PDC, or force clock steps from an alert. Time changes can disrupt authentication and distributed workloads. Preserve XML, command output, configuration source, network evidence, alert and disposition.

## Troubleshooting

- No rows: verify System input/provider/index/RBAC/forwarder and source health.
- Peer/error missing: inspect raw message/event data and locale; add tested extraction without dropping rows.
- Repeated 129: verify DC discovery, DNS/site records, domain hierarchy and connectivity.
- Repeated 134: validate exact manual peer spelling/resolution and UDP 123 request/response per Microsoft.
- Event 36: read the message's duration/provider context and current status; do not hard-code 24 hours for all versions/configurations.
- Event 142: determine whether the host should advertise and whether its clock is synchronized; server role matters.
- Authentication problems without rows: measure offset and inspect broader W32Time/Kerberos/network telemetry; this four-event rule is not complete.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for Windows saying that it cannot find or resolve a clock source, has gone too long without useful time, or has stopped offering time to other machines. Engineers then check the machine's real clock source and role before changing anything.
